title: The ideal h_A and resolutions of R -> A -> Lambda ⊃ q (Popescu's local problem)
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A$ an $R$-algebra of finite presentation ($A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$), $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras into a commutative ring $\Lambda$, and $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal. Put $\mathfrak h_A=\sqrt{H_{A/R}\Lambda}\subset\Lambda$, the radical of the ideal of $\Lambda$ generated by $\alpha(H_{A/R})$, where $H_{A/R}$ is the singular ideal of $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. A *resolution* of $R\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ is a factorization $A\xrightarrow{\beta}B\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda$ of $\alpha$ by homomorphisms of $R$-algebras with $B$ of finite presentation over $R$ ($B\cong R[y_1,\dots,y_k]/(g_1,\dots,g_l)$ as $R$-algebras) such that $\mathfrak h_A\subset\mathfrak h_B$ and $\mathfrak h_B\not\subset\mathfrak q$, where $\mathfrak h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}\Lambda}$ is formed with $\gamma$; $R\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ *can be resolved* if it has a resolution.

proof.text: (The ideal $\mathfrak h_A$.) For any ring map $R\to A$ the singular ideal $H_{A/R}\subset A$ is an ideal of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], defined from the $R$-algebra $A$ alone (the radical of the ideal generated by the $g\in A$ with $A_g$ smooth over $R$); it does not depend on a chosen presentation $A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$, and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $A\cong A'$ carries $H_{A/R}$ onto $H_{A'/R}$ (it carries the elements $g$ with $A_g$ smooth onto those with $A'_{g'}$ smooth). Hence $H_{A/R}\Lambda$, the set of finite sums $\sum\lambda_i\alpha(a_i)$ with $\lambda_i\in\Lambda$, $a_i\in H_{A/R}$, is an ideal of $\Lambda$ determined by $(R\to A,\alpha)$, and $\mathfrak h_A=\sqrt{H_{A/R}\Lambda}=\{\lambda\in\Lambda:\lambda^N\in H_{A/R}\Lambda\text{ for some }N\ge1\}$ is a radical ideal of $\Lambda$ (the radical of an ideal is an ideal: if $x^a,y^b\in I$ then $(x+y)^{a+b-1}\in I$ by the binomial formula, and $(\lambda x)^a=\lambda^ax^a\in I$).

(The ideal $\mathfrak h_B$ and the resolution condition.) Given a factorization $A\xrightarrow{\beta}B\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda$ of $\alpha$ by $R$-algebra maps ($\gamma\circ\beta=\alpha$) with $B$ of finite presentation over $R$, the data $R\to B\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ is again as in Situation 07F7 ($R$ Noetherian, $B$ of finite presentation, $\gamma$ an $R$-algebra map, $\mathfrak q$ a prime of $\Lambda$), so step 1 applied to it defines the radical ideal $\mathfrak h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}\Lambda}\subset\Lambda$, formed with $\gamma$. Both $\mathfrak h_A$ and $\mathfrak h_B$ are ideals of the same ring $\Lambda$, so '$\mathfrak h_A\subset\mathfrak h_B$' and '$\mathfrak h_B\not\subset\mathfrak q$' are meaningful conditions; Stacks' chain '$\mathfrak h_A\subset\mathfrak h_B\not\subset\mathfrak q$' means exactly their conjunction. The inclusion $\mathfrak h_A\subset\mathfrak h_B$ is a condition imposed, not a consequence of the factorization ($\beta$ need not map $H_{A/R}$ into $H_{B/R}$). 'Can be resolved' is the existence of such $(B,\beta,\gamma)$; it is unchanged if $B$ is replaced by an isomorphic $R$-algebra (step 1), and finite presentation of $B$ is the condition (i) of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], i.e. $B\cong R[y_1,\dots,y_k]/(g_1,\dots,g_l)$.

(What the definition does not contain.) Stacks states no property of $\mathfrak h_A$ or of resolutions together with the definition: the independence of $\mathfrak h_A$ of a presentation of $A$ is built into the intrinsic definition of $H_{A/R}$ (step 1), and no transitivity or composition lemma for resolutions is stated in Section 07F6. The statements that follow, Lemma Tag 07F8 (lemma-lift-solution: lifting a resolution modulo $(\pi_1^8,\dots,\pi_r^8)$), Lemma Tag 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak) and Lemma Tag 07FA (lemma-delocalize-height-zero: passing from a resolution at $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ to one over $R$), are theorems about resolutions used in the proofs of Lemmas Tag 07FE (lemma-resolve-special) and Tag 07FJ (lemma-resolve-general), i.e. below lem-weil-pbc-popescu-resolve-separable and lem-weil-pbc-popescu-resolve-char-p; they depend on this definition and are not used by it, so they belong to the splits of those nodes and are not created here. The Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ is part of the Situation (it is used by those lemmas) and is not used for the well-definedness in steps 1-2.

Three elementary steps: h_A is a well-defined radical ideal of Lambda (H_{A/R} intrinsic by def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal, independent of presentation and invariant under isomorphism; radical of an ideal is an ideal); h_B is formed with gamma in the same ring so the two resolution conditions are meaningful, and h_A in h_B is imposed, not automatic; and what the definition does not contain: Stacks records no property of h_A or of resolutions with the definition (no presentation-independence lemma, no transitivity lemma); 07F8, 07F9, 07FA are lemmas about resolutions used in 07FE/07FJ, below the resolve-separable/resolve-char-p nodes, so they belong to those splits. No new nodes. Mathlib: smoothLocus exists (as a set of primes), nothing on h_A or resolutions; recorded leansearch, leanfinder, loogle and grep.
